title: security.txt must contain a Contact field

spec.name: RFC 9116
spec.normative_quote: The "Contact" field indicates a method that researchers should use for reporting security vulnerabilities... At least one instance of this field MUST always be present in a "security.txt" file.
spec.note: Recalled from training-data familiarity with the published RFC, not re-verified against a live fetch this session (this agent has no WebFetch access). The deferred drift probe (ADR 0011 follow-up (h)) must reconcile this quote against a live re-fetch of spec.url before it is treated as verified. Raised from severity: warn to severity: fail in this change (decisions/0011) -- the live file (public/.well-known/security.txt) already has a Contact: line, so this is green today and carries no rollout risk; see policy_note.

policy_note: Prior to this change, check-security-txt.mjs:47-49 emitted this id at severity: warn while its own message cited '(required by RFC 9116 §2.5.1)' -- a genuine MUST mislabelled at a severity lib/http.mjs:44 never fails the check on. rule_class: conformance forces severity: fail (this schema's own constraint), which is what surfaces the mislabel and corrects it rather than relabelling the rule_class down to match the old severity.
applicability: A security.txt body of any length -- EXCEPT one whose Expires field is missing or unparseable, where security-txt-expires-missing / security-txt-expires-unparseable fire and return early (check-security-txt.mjs:19-23,27-34) before this check ever runs. The Deletion-Test rehearsal (decisions/0011, Step 4 AC) surfaced this as a real gap: a reimplementation guided only by an earlier, unqualified version of this sentence ('A security.txt body of any length') independently derived an unconditional Contact check and produced an extra security-txt-contact-missing finding on cases/no-expires.txt, which the declared case's expect (correctly) excludes.
expectation: The body contains at least one line matching /^Contact:\s*\S/ (case-insensitive). This check does not run at all when Expires is missing or unparseable -- see applicability.

cases.name: no Expires field -- this rule is inapplicable too (early return happens before the Contact check ever runs)
Contact field present -- this rule does not fire
